1.explanation:
1. MultiSelect.js – this is where the multiselect’s internal isOpen state is managed via Downshift’s onStateChange handler. It never calls back to the consumer when isOpen changes, so it must be updated to accept an onMenuChange prop and invoke it whenever the menu opens or closes (e.g. in the ToggleButtonClick and MenuBlur/MenuKeyDownEscape cases).
2. Dropdown.js – the single-select Dropdown shares the same Downshift setup and also manages its own isOpen state. To provide onMenuChange for all dropdown-style components, Dropdown.js should likewise accept onMenuChange and call it when isOpen toggles.
1.bug_scenario: Both gifs illustrate the problem: when the user clicks in the multiselect (the “Roles” dropdown) and makes selections, the menu opens and closes multiple times and there is no single callback fired when the menu visibility changes. The current workaround hacks focus/blur events and timeouts around the tags to detect when the menu has closed and the user is “done” with their selection. What’s needed is a built-in onMenuChange prop on the MultiSelect component (and by extension on the base Dropdown) that fires once when the menu opens or closes, so consumers don’t have to rely on brittle focus/blur hacks or timeouts.
